scope: Design-agent image direction only; no brand ingestion or library expansion

protocol.comparison: Freeze each source snapshot and record differences. The initial live comparison changes both guidance and reference-selection tools; it measures the combined system change, not a prompt-only causal effect. Keep briefs, source bytes and model configuration equal for the close-companion baseline and candidate.
protocol.inputs: Resolve fixture requirements to authorized current-run assets and record IDs and digests before either run. Fixture descriptions alone do not replace image inputs.
protocol.reference_delivery: Record both successful reference views and actual generation-input provenance. These are separate checks.
protocol.review: Inspect source and candidate pixels, then the native scene at delivery size. Record authoring quality separately from provider delivery and mechanical editability. No self-reported success substitutes for inspection.
protocol.timing: Measure request acceptance through saved usable artifact including queueing, image generation, inspection and repair. Distinguish prepared-asset reuse from fresh generation.
protocol.results: For each attempt record case ID, knowledge digest, model configuration, run/artifact IDs, actual source digests, operation, generated asset IDs, editability evidence, elapsed seconds, reviewer verdict and unmet requirements. Unavailable observations remain unknown.
protocol.repetition: Repeat representative passing cases to check that the result is not a single fortunate output. Test a different brand without changing the skill.
protocol.contrast: For native copy over raster imagery, record resolved foreground, mapped source-image copy region, input digest and measured threshold flags. Distinguish source-pixel sampling from full-composition/glyph evidence and inspect the final render.

fixture_requirements: Authorized abstract brand background with no identifiable landscape
Exact brand logo asset
cases.brief: Make two new background options in this reference's visual family for the same awareness message. Keep logo and headline separately editable.
observe: Views the actual reference
Chooses close companions and meaningful composition differences
Preserves abstract subject language and observed treatment
Keeps marketing text and logo out of generated artwork
Views both generated outputs and preserves usable alternatives
failure_examples: Invents a literal lake or forest from an abstract field
Counts the original as a new variant
Claims success from a provider status alone

fixture_requirements: Original product screenshot showing the advertised feature
Brand atmosphere reference
cases.brief: Explain this feature using our actual product screen and a newly generated background. The screen must remain authentic and replaceable.
observe: Inspects and reuses the relevant original screen
Generates only the requested background
Plans product and copy bounds together
Preserves native marketing text and independent original UI layer
failure_examples: Regenerates the complete dashboard
Adds unsupported product behavior
Uses an irrelevant screenshot merely because it is available

fixture_requirements: Brand reference with a distinctive photographic or illustrative treatment
Brief about a subject absent from current assets
cases.brief: Create a new visual concept explaining coordinated work. Our current photos do not depict this topic. Preserve the brand's visual treatment.
observe: Names why a new subject serves the message
Chooses new concept rather than forced source reuse
Describes specific observed treatment to carry forward
Separates a permitted subject change from an unsupported lighting, material or motif change
Can use a new arrangement of observed forms with native explanatory copy when a literal metaphor would change the brand's character
Does not present a metaphor as actual product functionality
failure_examples: Copies an irrelevant subject
Uses arbitrary atmosphere with no source-grounded treatment or stated role in the creative
Matches the palette and texture but invents a different lighting language to illustrate a campaign keyword
Invents a testimonial or result

fixture_requirements: Original matte textured brand field
Rejected generated companion that retained the pattern but invented luminous motifs
Existing scene with useful native copy and authentic logo
cases.brief: The pattern belongs to the brand, but the invented lighting does not. Create a new companion from the original visual language and preserve the editable foreground.
observe: Inspects the original source and the rejected candidate
Uses the original as the generation input rather than reinforcing the rejected treatment
Preserves distinct treatment dimensions instead of accepting a palette-only match
Views the generated component and final scene before accepting
Retains native foreground layers and reports any unrelated changes
failure_examples: Rationalizes unsupported lighting as a metaphor for the campaign
Sends the rejected image as the only reference for a new companion
Accepts conspicuous treatment drift because the dot pattern matches

fixture_requirements: Authorized exact product photo
Brand logo variant
cases.brief: Use this exact product photograph and this exact logo. Improve their arrangement while retaining their original appearance.
observe: Chooses original-asset reuse and native placement
Keeps exact logo uncropped
Avoids unnecessary generative modification of identity-critical pixels
failure_examples: Promises exact pixel identity from generative editing
Redraws the logo
Claims a new image was generated when the original was reused

fixture_requirements: Two visibly conflicting turn attachments
A desired library image that is not a turn attachment
cases.brief: Generate using only the library image's appearance and ignore the two attached images.
observe: Distinguishes viewing an asset from attaching it
Passes only the chosen authorized library asset with reference_asset_ids
Verifies returned input IDs and digests and preserves the turn attachment configuration
Reports unavailable selected bytes without spending on an unconditioned substitute
failure_examples: Leaves conflicting attachments implicitly selected
Describes a viewed image as a confirmed generation input without a receipt
Claims a placeholder was conditioned on selected references

fixture_requirements: A low-resolution textured reference where the precise production method is uncertain
cases.brief: Generate a companion with the same texture. Explain the visual qualities that need to carry forward.
observe: Describes visible pattern scale and tonal relationships
Marks uncertain effect identification
Checks texture after resizing to the intended placement
Does not claim an exact recovered shader/filter setting
failure_examples: Calls every noisy image a halftone
Asserts native dither or backdrop blur support that the tool does not expose

fixture_requirements: Brand illustration reference
Background that must remain visible behind a movable foreground

observe: Plans foreground bounds and overlap
Uses supported native paths/icons or clearly labels raster artwork
Checks actual alpha when available
Treats an opaque result as a failed cutout requirement
Keeps labels native

Places an opaque rectangle and claims transparency

fixture_requirements: An unavailable requested reference
A fixed existing run budget
cases.brief: Use this reference to create a matching background, but finish within the run budget.
observe: Reports unavailable pixels instead of inventing observations
Distinguishes unconditioned exploration from reference-matched generation
Preserves useful existing work
Reports unmet reference/generated-image requirements if necessary
failure_examples: Fabricates details of the missing reference
Retries identical cached requests indefinitely

fixture_requirements: Pale generated artwork below white editable copy
Authentic dark wordmark with no appropriate white wordmark in the kit
cases.brief: Repair legibility and remove logo treatment that resembles an unrequested CTA. Preserve useful imagery and authentic independent identity.
observe: Measures actual image regions instead of dismissing token contrast diagnostics
Repairs failing copy and checks final render
Checks the pixels of fetched logo variants, not just provider labels
Reports a missing authentic wordmark rather than redrawing it
failure_examples: Calls a pale chevron a full wordmark because its metadata says lockup
Accepts white copy on pale ground
Claims an added white plate matches a white reference wordmark
